result.title: The First-Order Value of Free Covariates in Budgeted Risk Monitoring
result.summary: A deployed model sees its inputs for free, but checking whether its risk has risen requires costly labels. We study how to spend a label budget so that a risk increase is detected quickly while false alarms stay controlled, including under input shifts that keep the risk below a safety threshold $τ$. Let $A$ be the false-alarm control scale and $h(r)=\mathrm{kl}(r,τ)$ the Bernoulli KL divergence between the changed risk $r$ and $τ$. At label rate $b=c/\log A$, we prove that every rule that chooses requests from its own label history has worst-case (Lorden) delay at least $(1/h(r)+1/c)\log A$ to first order: besides collecting evidence, it must wait for its next label. The bound needs only a label budget on one finite stretch of safe source data and false-alarm control over an initial window; a bound on the average time to false alarm does not suffice. When a harmful change also shifts the inputs, a rule that lets the inputs trigger labeling attains delay $\log A/h(r)$ to first order on a fixed Gaussian model, so free covariates save at least $1/b$ rounds. A hybrid rule adds a label-history fallback for risk changes that leave the inputs unchanged. Synthetic experiments and two ACS tasks, with strengthened label-only baselines, show the predicted pattern. The covariate trigger has a cost: because its budget is calibrated on the source, a benign input shift can make it request nearly every label.

AI.brief_summary: 研究仅输入免费、标签昂贵时如何分配标注预算，以尽快检测风险上升并控制误报，给出延迟下界，并比较输入触发标注与带标签历史回退的混合策略。
AI.relevance_reason: 其免费协变量触发标注及延迟—误报权衡，可能为 LVR 中何时调用视觉证据与 LOOK/STOP 的停止判据提供概念参照；但统计监控设定距多模态推理较远，迁移性待核查。
